NFL DFS Week 2 Picks: Top DraftKings Projections, Values and Sim Plays

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, September 20 · 13 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of September 20, 3:22 PM ET

Christian McCaffrey carries the highest SPAGS model projection on the Week 2 DraftKings main slate: 23.5 DraftKings points at $8,000. He holds 30% of the simulated winning-lineup credit across 10,000 simulations. Bijan Robinson holds the largest share at 34% for $8,200.

Behind McCaffrey, the model's next four projections are Bijan Robinson (23.2, $8,200), Derrick Henry (21.1, $7,200), Chase Brown (19.4, $6,900) and Ja'Marr Chase (19.3, $7,600). Christian McCaffrey returns the most per dollar of that group at 2.94 projected points per $1,000. Ja'Marr Chase leads the wide receivers at 19.3 for $7,600, Brock Purdy leads the quarterbacks at 18.8 for $6,200, and Trey McBride leads the tight ends at 16.0 for $6,900.

The 13-game slate runs from a 50.5-point total in WAS at DAL down to 39.5 in PHI at TEN. Every projection below is a SPAGS model estimate from the September 20, 3:22 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. Winning-lineup credit comes from 10,000 simulations of the contest, and tied winning entries share credit. A player's simulated floor is his 10th-percentile score and his ceiling is his 95th.

Quarterbacks: Week 2 DraftKings projections

Brock Purdy, SF vs MIA ($6,200)

Brock Purdy carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 18.8 DraftKings points at $6,200. That is 0.1 points clear of Drake Maye. The model includes 3.5 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.02 projected points per $1,000, 10th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Purdy averaged 18.8 points with a simulated floor of 7.3 and a ceiling of 34.3, and he holds 9% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 13.5-point favorite at home against Miami, with an implied team total of 29 in a game totaled at 44.5.

Drake Maye, NE vs PIT ($6,100)

Drake Maye projects 2nd at the position with 18.7 DraftKings points at $6,100. The model includes 5.0 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.06 projected points per $1,000, 9th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Maye averaged 18.6 points with a simulated floor of 7.3 and a ceiling of 34.1, and he holds 6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. New England is a 5.5-point favorite at home against Pittsburgh, with an implied team total of 23.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.

Value: Drew Lock, SEA at ARI ($4,900)

Drew Lock projects for 17.4 DraftKings points at $4,900, which works out to 3.56 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 21 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 5.7 rushing attempts. The current projection of 17.4 compares with a saved model baseline of 0.0. Across 10,000 simulations Lock averaged 17.3 points with a simulated floor of 6.9 and a ceiling of 31.2, and he holds 3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Seattle is a 3.5-point favorite on the road against Arizona, with an implied team total of 22.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.
